stem: Why is it generally not advisable for a child under the age of four to use a large volume spacer?

options.text: The tidal volume required to clear the spacer is too great for a small child.
The weight of the device causes the mask to leak at the chin.
Large volume spacers are only compatible with adult-sized $PMDI$ canisters.
The plastic in larger spacers contains higher levels of static electricity.

explanation: Younger children do not take large enough breaths to effectively move all the medication out of a large chamber and into their lungs.
rationale: Consider the amount of air a small child moves in and out during a single breath.

optionExplanations.A: Younger children do not take large enough breaths to effectively move all the medication out of a large chamber and into their lungs.
optionExplanations.B: While seal is important, the primary physiological limitation is the child's breathing capacity relative to the chamber size.
optionExplanations.C: Most spacers are designed with universal ports that fit standard $PMDI$ canisters regardless of volume.
optionExplanations.D: Static is a property of the material and maintenance, not specifically the volume of the device.
